_comment: Self-consistent 2-core K1 config. The merlin dispatch_scheduler executes a schedule on exactly two worker pools (CPU_P and CPU_E), each pinned to the cpu ids given on the command line. Declaring 8 machines while running with --cpu_p_cpu_ids=0 --cpu_e_cpu_ids=4 over-subscribes 4 scheduler machines onto 1 physical core, which is what produced 87.6% queueing and 31/32 MLP deadline misses in the 8-machine run. One machine per pool, timed with single-core (topo_0) profiles, is the configuration the runtime can actually honour.
_capabilities_comment: IME is measured, not assumed: smt.vmadot executes on cores 0-3 and SIGILLs on 4-7 (artifacts/k1_bringup/*/ime_capability_probe.txt). It is therefore a property of cluster-0 cores, never a separate machine -- see xpu-rt/capabilities.py.
_concurrency_comment: machine_combination_mode=singletons: each of the 8 cores is independently schedulable, so 8 dispatches can genuinely run at once. This is why the profiles above are single-core (topo_0).
